summary: In March 2025, NASA-funded lander Athena tipped over near the Moon's south pole: the very low sun cast long shadows that confused its landing system. Since 2019, 12 landers have tried to land on the Moon and only 5 stayed upright, and the next south-pole landing (Artemis IV) will carry people. You can't rehearse on the Moon, so we find where on Earth you can. Using NASA LRO LOLA terrain, we measure the dangers that hurt real landers (long low-sun shadows, crater-rim height jumps, ground too featureless for camera navigation, and slope) for each of NASA's 9 candidate Artemis regions. Then we screen about 12,000 bare-land squares across Earth with the same measurements. For each region and danger we return the top 3 Earth matches, plus the dates and times when the sun sits at the matching low angle there. Our Moon shadows agree with NASA's own illumination map (r = 0.98), and for 33 of our 57 sites we found no prior analog study in the catalogs and literature we checked.
details:
What it does

Rehearse Here finds places on Earth where lunar landing and surface teams can rehearse under the same terrain and lighting dangers as NASA's 9 candidate Artemis south-pole regions.

  1. Danger profile per Moon region. From NASA LRO LOLA 20 m elevation data, we measure four dangers tied to real failures: low-sun shadows (IM-2 Athena), crater-rim height jumps (Hakuto-R), ground too featureless for camera navigation (Ingenuity), and slope.
  2. Global Earth screen. About 12,000 bare-land 15 km squares (about 2.7 million km², 15% of Earth's bare land) are measured the same way on Copernicus 30 m terrain. ESA WorldCover keeps only bare ground. A 30 m second stage and a NASADEM cross-check refine the best candidates.
  3. Top 3 per region × danger, each with rehearsal windows: the dates and local times when the sun is at the matching low angle (Astropy).
  4. Astronaut-walk matching. Draw a route on a Moon region and get an Earth path with the same ups and downs (72% exact recovery in a hidden-copy test).
  5. Ranking. The 9 regions are ordered from easiest to hardest to rehearse on Earth, with the weakest danger named for each.
  6. Alberta and Calgary view. We screened every 15 km square in Alberta. Kohler Coulee, 100 km south of Calgary, is Alberta's best shadow match for Mons Mouton Plateau. Moon walks are matched to City of Calgary pathways, prioritised with the Calgary Equity Index for public outreach.

How we validated it

  • Our computed Moon shadows match NASA's PGDA illumination map at r = 0.98.
  • Known analog sites beat random decoys (AUC 0.80).
  • Results are stable when the weights change by ±20% (88% overlap).
  • Every novelty claim is checked against the USGS and NASA analog catalogs and the literature. 33 of 57 sites have no prior analog study we could find.

Benefits and impact

These are cheap, safe, reachable rehearsal sites for landing-system tests, rover and astronaut traverse practice, and camera-navigation testing. Every site comes with a data-backed explanation of what matches and what doesn't. Two NASA-funded landers (IM-1 and IM-2, $172M in task orders) tipped over after landing; a week of Earth rehearsal costs a tiny fraction of that.

Honest limits

30 m terrain can't see boulders. Sky light fills Earth's shadows. Earth has no lunar gravity, vacuum or −200 °C nights. Some sites are in protected or remote areas (each is flagged).

Tools

Python (rasterio, numpy, astropy), React, TypeScript, three.js, Vite, Vercel. Code: https://github.com/felix101930/NASA-SPACE-APPS
dataRefs: LRO LOLA south-pole 20 m DEM (PGDA product 90, Barker et al. 2023): terrain for all 9 Artemis regions
LOLA south-pole illumination map (PGDA product 69, Mazarico et al. 2011): validates our Moon shadows, r = 0.98
NASA Artemis III candidate landing regions: locations of the 9 regions
NASADEM: cross-check of Earth terrain heights
MODIS MCD43C3 albedo: ground brightness vs the Moon region
Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLS): satellite images of Earth sites
NASA GIBS imagery: map imagery of Earth sites
NASA 3D Resources: models in the pitch
projectRefs: ESA/Airbus Copernicus DEM GLO-30 and GLO-90: Earth terrain
NRCan HRDEM 1 m lidar: Calgary terrain
Protected Planet WDPCA (UNEP-WCMC, IUCN): protected areas
City of Calgary Open Data and Calgary Equity Index 2024
